safety: Never quote a firm system price by phone — the band is $4,500-$12,000 for complete French drain + sump systems and the real number comes from the free on-site assessment
Never invent prices, discounts, warranty terms, deposit or financing details — anything marked [CONFIRM WITH OWNER] must be confirmed before quoting
Never claim insurance will cover the work or advise on coverage — homeowners policies generally exclude gradual seepage; say that and stop
Never promise protection against hurricane storm surge or river flooding above the slab — the system fights groundwater and storm soak, be honest about the line
Never diagnose a yard you have not seen — the assessment exists because every lot's soil, slope, and water table differ
Never invent customer names, review counts, or guaranteed outcomes
Never teach fake urgency or fake deadlines — Florida's wet season and named storms are real urgency enough
No scare tactics — state real risks plainly (foundation, mold, resale) without dramatizing
Respect do-not-call requests immediately and log them
No auto-send: every outbound draft requires human approval in the desk

FrenchDrain.label: French Drains
FrenchDrain.tagline: Engineered, not guessed — perimeter systems that lower the water around your foundation.
FrenchDrain.icp: Central Florida homeowners with chronic standing water, soggy yards days after rain, water at the foundation or lanai; flat lots; high-water-table neighborhoods (Port Orange, Daytona, NSB, Ormond, Sanford, Orlando, DeLand, Deltona).
FrenchDrain.not_icp: Renters (route to landlord/PropertyMgmt), storm-surge/river flooding cases (be honest — not our fight), homes with a one-time surface puddle that drains in an hour (YardDrainage or no-sale honesty).
FrenchDrain.offer: Exterior French drain: fabric-lined trench, clean gravel, 4-inch perforated pipe, custom trench/slope/discharge design, typically 150-350 linear feet, usually paired with a sump basin + pump for discharge on flat lots. Includes full landscape restoration — invisible when done.
FrenchDrain.pricing: Complete French drain + sump systems typically $4,500-$12,000 depending on trench length, sump needs, and discharge run. Quoted ONLY after the free on-site assessment. Most quotes land mid-band, not the top.
FrenchDrain.payment_terms: [CONFIRM WITH OWNER] — never state deposit, financing, or payment-method details until confirmed.
FrenchDrain.turnaround: Free assessment scheduled within 24 hours; many residential installs complete in 1-3 days depending on access, soil, and scope.
discovery: After a hard rain, how long does water stand?
Has water reached the foundation, lanai, or inside?
What have you already tried — regrading, gutters, a trench?
How long have you owned the home — any plans to sell?

objections.just_regrade: Regrading moves the puddle; it cannot lower a water table sitting 2-6 feet down. Chronic groundwater needs subsurface collection (fabric, gravel, pipe) plus pumped discharge.
objections.too_expensive: The assessment is free — get the real number for YOUR yard. Anchor against foundation repair ($10k+), mold remediation, yearly re-sodding, and failed inspections at resale.
objections.insurance: Homeowners policies exclude gradual seepage and groundwater damage. Flood insurance pays after a disaster — it doesn't prevent the damage or the claims history.
objections.landscaper: Filter fabric, slope math, pump sizing, and code-compliant discharge separate a system from a ditch that clogs in a year in Florida sand. And we warranty the work.
objections.after_hurricane_season: Dry-season installs are easier on the yard and you're protected before the water arrives.
objections.selling_soon: A wet crawlspace kills inspections. A dry yard is a listing asset.

dns.A_urgent: 85-100: water is touching the structure or standing for days. Talk track: lead with the specific signals, the compounding-damage frame, and book the assessment within 24-48 hours.
dns.B_urgent: 70-84: strong chronic signals. Talk track: neighborhood social proof + wet-season timing, close a concrete slot this week.
dns.C_priority: 50-69: recurring but not structural yet. Talk track: 'cheaper to fix before it reaches the slab' — offer the free assessment as a no-risk fact-finding step.
dns.D_monitor: 30-49: intermittent surface pooling. Talk track: YardDrainage entry offer, keep on nurture for wet season.
dns.F_monitor: 0-29: little evidence of need. Be honest, offer seasonal check-in, do not push.

SumpPump.label: Sump Pumps
SumpPump.tagline: The active defense — because flat Florida lots give gravity nowhere to go.
SumpPump.icp: Homes with damp/wet crawlspaces, musty smells, mold worries, flat lots, existing French drains without discharge, garages/AC pads that take on water; landlords with tenant complaints.
SumpPump.not_icp: Yards with pure surface pooling and healthy slope (YardDrainage), storm-surge exposure sold as 'flood proofing' (never).
SumpPump.offer: Interior drains routed to a sealed sump basin; submersible pump with float switch; check valve; discharge line 10-20+ feet from the foundation to a code-compliant location. Battery backup and smart monitoring options — hurricanes cut power exactly when groundwater peaks.
SumpPump.pricing: Scoped per home; often part of a complete $4,500-$12,000 system. Battery backup and monitoring are add-ons every Florida homeowner should hear about. Quote only after the free assessment.
SumpPump.turnaround: Free assessment within 24 hours; installs commonly 1-2 days.
discovery: Any musty smell, mold, or damp insulation under the house?
Does the yard stay wet days after rain?
What happens at your place when a storm knocks out power?
Existing pump? When was it last tested?

objections.overkill: On a flat lot gravity has nowhere to send water. The pump is what actually moves it away — everything else just collects it.
objections.power_outage: That's why we spec battery backup — the storm cutting your power is the same storm pushing groundwater at your foundation.
objections.have_pump: Float switches stick and check valves fail silently. We test, service, and upgrade systems we didn't install.
objections.mold_fear: Moisture under the house feeds mold and rots framing. Drying the crawlspace is the fix; treatment without drainage is a bandage.

dns.format: Same DNS format; musty smell / crawlspace signals push scores up.
dns.note: Crawlspace + mold signals usually score B or higher — book fast.

SumpPump.crm_status_path: New → Contacted → Assessment booked → Assessed/Quoted → Won | Lost
SumpPump.close_discipline: Close the free crawlspace + yard assessment. Existing-pump mentions convert to inspection visits, upgrades, and Maintenance plans.
never: Mold-remediation promises (we fix the water, not the spores)

YardDrainage.label: Yard Drainage
YardDrainage.tagline: Get the lanai back — surface water gone in hours, not days.
YardDrainage.icp: Flooded lanais/patios, pooling driveways, dead-grass low spots, downspouts dumping at the slab, erosion at beds and retaining walls, mosquito ponds.
YardDrainage.not_icp: Chronic groundwater/water-table cases (French drain conversation), structural flooding (be honest).
YardDrainage.offer: Catch basins, channel drains, swales, downspout tie-ins, precision re-grading; routed to safe discharge — often the same sump or storm connection as a French drain system. Landscape protected and restored.
YardDrainage.pricing: Scope varies by yard — lower entry ticket than full systems; quoted at the free assessment. Often the first job that becomes a full system later.
YardDrainage.turnaround: Free assessment within 24 hours; most surface jobs are quick installs.
discovery: Where exactly does water collect — lanai, driveway, low spot?
How long before it drains on its own?
Where do your downspouts dump?
Erosion, dead grass, or mosquitoes?

objections.eventually_drains: Days of standing water kills grass, breeds mosquitoes, and soaks soil against the slab. 'Eventually' is damage in slow motion.
objections.too_expensive: Surface drainage is our most affordable work — and the assessment that scopes it is free.
objections.add_dirt: New dirt without an engineered flow path moves the pool somewhere else — often closer to the house.

dns.note: Surface-only signals usually score C-D — sell the entry offer, watch for groundwater signals that upgrade the conversation.

YardDrainage.close_discipline: Fast close on the free assessment — lowest-friction offer in the lineup. The upsell to a full system happens on-site, never on the phone.
never: Overselling a full system when surface work solves it — honesty converts neighbors

Maintenance.label: Maintenance
Maintenance.tagline: Storm-ready, every season — because pumps fail silently.
Maintenance.icp: Anyone with an existing sump or French drain (ours or inherited), past FloGuard customers, sellers prepping inspections, property managers.
Maintenance.not_icp: Homes with no drainage infrastructure at all (that's an assessment conversation, not a plan).
Maintenance.offer: Seasonal storm-readiness service: pump test, basin inspection/cleaning, discharge + check-valve check, battery health, recommendations; monitoring options that alert on excessive run time or power loss. FloGuard services systems it did not install.
Maintenance.pricing: Plan pricing: [CONFIRM WITH OWNER] — never invent a number. Frame against what a silent pump failure costs in the first storm of the season.
Maintenance.turnaround: Book service visits late spring, before the May-October wet season; urgent post-storm issues prioritized.
discovery: When was the pump last tested or serviced?
Installed it, or inherited it with the house?
Battery backup — how old is the battery?
Plans to sell in the next couple of years?

objections.test_myself: The monthly bucket test is great — keep it. Our visit covers what you can't see: basin sediment, a sticking float, a tired battery, a blocked discharge line.
objections.been_fine: Pumps fail silently — right up until the first big storm of the season.
objections.not_your_install: We service inherited systems all the time — inspect, repair, or bring it to storm-ready standard.

dns.note: Maintenance leads aren't scored on need — timing is the lever: pre-season beats post-storm.

Maintenance.crm_status_path: New → Contacted → Visit booked → Serviced → Plan active | Lost
Maintenance.close_discipline: Book the seasonal visit on a specific date — late spring ideally. Recurring plan close beats one-off visit. Batteries every 2-3 years is the natural re-touch.
never: Scare tactics — the first-storm story is real enough

PropertyMgmt.label: Property Mgmt (B2B)
PropertyMgmt.tagline: One vendor, scheduled seasons, fewer tenant complaints.
PropertyMgmt.icp: Property management companies, HOA boards, landlords with multiple rentals, vacation-rental managers across Central Florida.
PropertyMgmt.not_icp: Single-home owners (homeowner playbooks), commercial civil-engineering scale projects (refer out honestly).
PropertyMgmt.offer: Portfolio drainage programs: pilot assessment of the worst property with a written scope for the owner, prioritized fixes, seasonal maintenance across the portfolio, one vendor, clean invoicing, scheduled service.
PropertyMgmt.pricing: Per-property scoping after the pilot walk-through; portfolio programs in a simple agreement. Numbers: [CONFIRM WITH OWNER]. Never invent volume discounts.
PropertyMgmt.payment_terms: [CONFIRM WITH OWNER] — invoicing terms for management companies to be confirmed.
PropertyMgmt.turnaround: Pilot walk-through within the week; written scope suitable to forward to owners.
discovery: How many doors, and which properties flood?
What do drainage complaints cost per season — calls, visits, turnover?
Who approves maintenance spend — you or the owners?
One-off fixes today, or would a scheduled seasonal program help?

objections.owners_approve: Start with one free pilot assessment and a written scope you can hand the owner — real numbers, their call, you look prepared.
objections.have_handyman: Handymen patch symptoms. Chronic drainage is an engineering problem and returns every wet season until the water has somewhere to go.
objections.too_busy: That's the pitch: one vendor, scheduled seasonal service, no more 2am emergency calls during a tropical storm.
